Anya: Heads-up: we need a concrete approach for resumable partial streams that balances memory and determinism. Current options blow either memory or correctness.

Kevin: Agreed. Quick taxonomy: per-chunk ACKs, short-lived edge buffer + signed resume token, persistent checkpointing in KV.

Maria: Per-chunk ACKs require client changes (ACKs every N bytes) which breaks many SDKs. Signed tokens sound pragmatic if we accept a window.

Jonathan: What about capturing minimal runtime state? We could 1) keep kvcache fingerprints (not full cache) + token; 2) if fingerprint mismatch, fail fast to restart. Cheap and safer than full cache snapshot.

Kevin: Nice. Fingerprint approach avoids heavy storage but detects incompatibility. If mismatch, return 409 + suggested fallback URL.

Anya: Backpressure: enforce per-conn buffer cap and emit X-Stream-Window on start. If client slower than window, gateway evicts earliest bytes and marks token invalid.

Maria: Headers proposal: X-Resume-Token, X-Partial-Offset, X-Idempotent:true|false, server sends X-Stream-Window: 20s. Use 206 to indicate resumed partial content.

sre-bot: alert: staging rollout queued for edge-resume-v1 (canary).

Jonathan: Tests: slow-client farm, cross-tenant token replay, fingerprint mismatch, billing on restart. Also measure perf delta for 95p latency.

Anya: Action items: Maria drafts token format + HMAC scheme; Kevin prototypes per-conn budget + eviction policy; Jonathan writes RFC skeleton. We'll reconvene in 48h.

Kevin: I'll post a short PoC curl example when ready.
